guidelines.title: too few options radios not dropdown
guidelines.rule: Too few options → radios, not dropdown (NN/g “handful” / ~under 5; DS cutoffs cited on-page: USWDS <7, M3 6, Carbon 3).

citation.source: NN/g — Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?

pass_when: A handful of options (~under 5; other cited DS cutoffs on-page) is radios, not a dropdown.
fail_when: Two–few options hidden in a dropdown.
guidelines.do_not_claim: One house cutoff that collapses NN/g handful vs USWDS <7 vs M3 6 vs Carbon 3 vs Polar <4. Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.inputs.match_control_and_size`, `dropdown_chooser`, `combo_box`, `offer_choices_not_only_text`.

guidelines.title: too many combobox not long dropdown
guidelines.rule: Too many (~15+) → combobox, not a long dropdown.

citation.source: NN/g — Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?

pass_when: A ~15+ set is a combobox (type + list), not a long dropdown.
fail_when: A long dropdown of ~15+ with no type-to-find.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Apple combo-box pairing (`forms.inputs.combo_box`) as a duplicate; a house “15” as law.

guidelines.title: familiar values type not dropdown
guidelines.rule: Highly familiar/predictable values → type, not dropdown.

citation.source: NN/g — Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?

pass_when: Familiar/predictable values (e.g. name-like known strings) are typed.
fail_when: Those values are only in a dropdown.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Autocompletion suggestions as this row.

guidelines.title: dropdown ok narrow middle
guidelines.rule: Dropdown OK in a narrow middle (~5–10) when the field is secondary or compactness matters.

citation.source: NN/g — Does Your Form Really Need a Dropdown List?

pass_when: A ~5–10 secondary/compact field may use a dropdown.
fail_when: Treating “dropdown never” or “dropdown always” as the rule for this middle band.
guidelines.do_not_claim: GOV.UK select-last-resort as a winner over this band.

guidelines.title: listbox vs dropdown
guidelines.rule: Dropdown to downplay alternatives / keep a default; listbox to expose options and encourage change.
pass_when: Dropdown is used to keep a default / downplay alternatives; listbox is used when options should stay visible and change is encouraged.
fail_when: Listbox hides alternatives that should stay visible, or a dropdown is used when the design needs to encourage changing the default.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Radio vs dropdown (separate rows).

guidelines.title: keyboard typeahead in dropdowns
guidelines.rule: Keyboard typeahead in dropdowns; avoid dropdown when typing is faster (state/country).
pass_when: Dropdowns support typeahead; state/country (typing faster) is not a dropdown.
fail_when: Dropdown with no typeahead, or state/country forced through a dropdown.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Mobile checkout “open field not iOS picker” as this row (see `nng.open-field-state-and-card-expiry`).

guidelines.title: avoid cascading dropdowns
guidelines.rule: Avoid cascading/interdependent dropdowns (options that appear/disappear from another widget).
pass_when: Choice sets are not chained so that a second dropdown’s options appear/disappear from the first.
fail_when: Interdependent dropdowns where the next list is populated only by the previous widget.
guidelines.do_not_claim: GOV.UK conditional reveal of a related question (different pattern).

guidelines.title: checkboxes multi radios exclusive
guidelines.rule: Checkboxes = independent multi; radios = mutually exclusive exactly-one.
pass_when: Independent multi uses checkboxes; exactly-one uses radios.
fail_when: Checkboxes for mutually exclusive exactly-one, or radios for independent multi.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Visuals (next row); GOV.UK “don’t assume from visuals alone”.

guidelines.title: standard visuals checkbox square radio circle
guidelines.rule: Standard visuals: checkbox square; radio circle with solid inner.
pass_when: Checkboxes are squares; radios are circles with a solid inner when selected.
fail_when: Swapped or nonstandard shapes that make the two indistinguishable.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Brand icon swaps as a house exception.

guidelines.title: vertical one choice per line
guidelines.rule: Vertical one-choice-per-line; space carefully if horizontal.
pass_when: Choices are stacked one per line, or a horizontal row is carefully spaced so each label maps to one control.
fail_when: Crowded horizontal choices that attach the wrong label to a control.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Hit-target px floors.

guidelines.title: prefer radios over dropdowns when visible
guidelines.rule: Prefer radios over dropdowns when options can stay visible.
pass_when: A set that can stay visible is radios (or equivalent exposed list), not a dropdown.
fail_when: Options that fit on screen are hidden in a dropdown.
guidelines.do_not_claim: The ~5–10 secondary compactness exception (`nng.dropdown-ok-narrow-middle`).

guidelines.title: radio set comprehensive other type in
guidelines.rule: Radio set must be comprehensive; add Other + type-in if not.
pass_when: Every valid answer is in the set, or Other + type-in covers the rest.
fail_when: Set is incomplete and there is no Other + type-in.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Silent preselect of a guessed Other.

guidelines.title: always select one radio by default
guidelines.rule: Always select one radio by default (users cannot return to “none”). Dual-cite with GOV.UK no-preselect-on-questions and Polar default-when-possible: satisfy “always one selected” with explicit None when none is valid — do not force a guessed answer.

citation.source: NN/g — Radio Buttons: Select One by Default

pass_when: The radio set has a selected value. If “none” is valid, that value is an explicit None. Settings: current/safe default.
fail_when: No selected radio (stuck with no way back to none, or an empty set); or a guessed real answer is preselected on a question where none/unknown is valid; or a global always/never with no question-vs-settings split.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A winner over GOV.UK questions or Polar “Select” placeholder when no logical default. Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.inputs.good_defaults_smart_prefills`.

guidelines.title: users rarely change defaults
guidelines.rule: Users rarely change defaults — pick most common/safe, not first-alpha; don’t always default the most expensive.
pass_when: Default is the common or safe value, not alphabetical-first and not automatically the most expensive.
fail_when: First-alpha or most-expensive default with no common/safe basis.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Question silent-preselect (locked dual-cite); Tidwell Good Defaults as a merge.

guidelines.title: eas framework
guidelines.rule: EAS framework (named): Eliminate → Automate → Simplify (one row, not a re-dump of keep-short / device features).
pass_when: Form effort is attacked in that order: eliminate, then automate, then simplify what remains.
fail_when: The named order is inverted (simplify first while still asking for eliminable/automatable data).
guidelines.do_not_claim: Re-listing `keep_short` / `use_device_features` / `compute_from_other_info` as this row. Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.length.keep_short`, `compute_from_other_info`, `use_device_features`. One named EAS row only.

guidelines.title: show the rules
guidelines.rule: Show the Rules — requirements visible the whole time the field is selected (not a hidden link; not inside the placeholder).

citation.source: NN/g — Password Creation: 3 Ways To Make It Easier

pass_when: While the password-creation field is selected, the requirements stay visible outside the placeholder.
fail_when: Rules only in a hidden link, only in the placeholder, or only after submit.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Strength meter (`forms.inputs.password_strength_meter`). Overlap with Forms 54: `forms.inputs.password_strength_meter` + `forms.fields.explain_format_upfront`. Meter already skipped; this row is requirements visible the whole time the field is selected.

guidelines.title: show the input password creation
guidelines.rule: Show the Input — unmask: desktop hidden by default + “Show password”; mobile/tablet shown by default + hide control. Separate from login (two checks, not a fight).

citation.source: NN/g — Password Creation: 3 Ways To Make It Easier

pass_when: Creation on mobile/tablet: value shown by default with a hide control. Desktop creation: masked by default with Show password.
fail_when: Mobile/tablet creation starts masked with no hide/show path that matches shown-by-default; desktop creation has no Show; or login’s mask-by-default is treated as this creation row.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Login masking (`nng.login-mask-plus-show-password`); never-prepopulate-password.

guidelines.title: dont repeat password email fields
guidelines.rule: Don’t repeat password/email fields; confirm on a later page instead.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Registration and Login Forms on Mobile

pass_when: Email and password are each asked once; confirmation is a later page, not a second identical field.
fail_when: Confirm-email or confirm-password duplicate fields on the same form.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Login Show password.

guidelines.title: login mask plus show password
guidelines.rule: Login: mask by default + Show password (differs from creation-on-mobile). Two checks, not a fight.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Registration and Login Forms on Mobile

pass_when: Login password is masked by default and has Show password.
fail_when: Login shown-by-default with no mask, or masked with no Show.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Mobile creation shown-by-default as a contradiction of this row.

guidelines.title: forgot password link
guidelines.rule: Forgot password link on every login.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Registration and Login Forms on Mobile

pass_when: Every login surface has a forgot-password link.
fail_when: Login with no forgot-password path.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Recovery-flow copy quality.

guidelines.title: alt registration and biometric login
guidelines.rule: Alt registration (social/federated) + biometric login where the platform has it.

citation.source: NN/g — A Checklist for Registration and Login Forms on Mobile

pass_when: Federated/social registration is offered; biometric login is offered where the platform has it.
fail_when: Platform has the capability and neither alt registration nor biometric is offered when this checklist applies.
guidelines.do_not_claim: That every product must ship every social provider.

guidelines.title: guest checkout prominent
guidelines.rule: Guest checkout prominent (above sign-in); optional password in-flow; mark password optional; user-benefit copy not newsletter pitch.

citation.source: NN/g — Don’t Force Users to Register Before They Can Buy; NN/g — The Mobile Checkout Experience

pass_when: Guest checkout is prominent and above sign-in; password in-flow is optional and labeled optional; copy states user benefit, not a newsletter pitch.
fail_when: Forced register-before-buy; guest buried under sign-in; password required in-flow; newsletter pitch as the reason.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Paywalled 137-rec report.

guidelines.title: cart easy remove no extra update
guidelines.rule: Cart: easy Remove per line; no extra Update button to commit quantity.
pass_when: Each line has easy Remove; quantity commits without a separate Update button.
fail_when: Remove is hard to find, or quantity needs an extra Update to commit.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Undo snackbar (see `nng.support-undo-discoverable`).

guidelines.title: order summary easy to find mobile
guidelines.rule: Order summary easy to find on mobile (not only below the fold).
pass_when: On mobile checkout, order summary is findable without only living below the fold.
fail_when: Summary only below the fold with no easy way to find it.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A required sticky-bar implementation.

guidelines.title: open field state and card expiry
guidelines.rule: Open field, not iOS picker/dropdown, for state and card expiry.
pass_when: State and card expiry are open fields (typeable), not iOS pickers/dropdowns.
fail_when: State or expiry uses a picker/dropdown as the only entry.
guidelines.do_not_claim: All dropdowns everywhere (see choice-cutoff rows).

guidelines.title: mobile friendly payment options
guidelines.rule: Mobile-friendly payment options without overwhelming; photo-to-fill card; cross-device cart.
pass_when: Payment options stay usable on mobile without an overwhelming list; card can be filled from a photo; cart works across devices.
fail_when: Overwhelming payment list, no photo-to-fill where the article’s pattern applies, or cart that cannot continue on another device.
guidelines.do_not_claim: A required set of named wallets.

guidelines.title: modal and nonmodal dialogs
guidelines.rule: Modal & Nonmodal Dialogs (7 numbered): (1) Important warnings / prevent or correct critical errors. (2) Request info critical to continuing the current process. (3) May fragment a complex workflow into simpler steps. (4) Ask for info that, if provided, significantly lessens work. (5) Do not use for nonessential, off-flow information. (6) Avoid interrupting high-stake processes such as checkout. (7) Avoid when the decision needs sources unavailable inside the modal.
pass_when: A modal is used for 1–4; not used for 5–7 (nonessential off-flow; interrupting checkout; decision needs outside sources).
fail_when: Modal for nonessential/off-flow; modal interrupting checkout; modal that needs sources not inside it; or no modal when a critical warning / critical-to-continue request applies.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Confirmation-dialog copy (`actions.confirm.*`); form-error-only-in-modal (`forms.errors.modal_not_only_copy`); Polar complex-form modal (dual-cite, keep both named).

guidelines.title: support undo discoverable
guidelines.rule: Support Undo that stays discoverable — visible control; snackbar-only undo that vanishes in seconds is a miss. Always allow Back; cancel in-progress. (Heuristic #3 not filed as a catalog row.)
pass_when: Undo is a discoverable visible control (not only a vanishing snackbar); Back is available; in-progress work can be cancelled.
fail_when: Undo only as a seconds-long snackbar; no Back; no cancel in-progress.
guidelines.do_not_claim: Heuristic #3 as a row; `actions.multilevel_undo` / `actions.cancelability` as merges. Overlap with Actions 40: `multilevel_undo` / `cancelability`.
